response_text:
Looking at this PR carefully, I need to check the actual logic and whether tests would catch the issues.

Let me trace through the code paths:

**UsernameForm.java line 47**: Calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only definition in the parent class `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. This won't compile.

**UsernamePasswordForm.java lines 115-117**: The new condition `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` requires `user != null` (the helper enforces this), so `fillContextForm` is never called when user is null. The original code called `fillContextForm` unconditionally when passkeys were enabled at realm level (inside the `else` branch when user was null).

Let me verify the regression breaks the existing test `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` (which was modified only stylistically, not in its assertions about the webauthn form). It still asserts `driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"))` is `notNullValue()` even on the first login page when user is null. With the new code, `fillContextForm` won't run when user is null, so `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI` won't be set and the webauthn form won't render.

There is no no-arg overload defined anywhere in the codebase, so this line fails to compile and the PR cannot be built. The caller almost certainly meant `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`."}, {"file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java", "line": 115, "severity": "high", "category": "bug", "title": "Conditional passkeys UI not initialized on initial (user-less) login", "body": "The new check `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))` relies on a helper that includes `user != null` in its predicate. As a result `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never invoked when the user has not yet been identified on the first visit to the username/password form. The pre-PR code (inside the `else` branch) unconditionally called `fillContextForm` when `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`, which is the behavior the existing test `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest#passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` (and the equivalent test in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest`) still relies on. Both tests assert that `//form[@id='webauth']` is present and that `usernameAutocomplete` equals `\"username webauthn\"` on the very first login page before any user is set, so this regression will make those tests fail. The intent of the PR is to add passkey support for re-authentication (user already present), not to remove it for the initial login. The fix is to gate `fillContextForm` on `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` only, dropping the user-presence requirement (or splitting the helper into a realm-level predicate and a user-level predicate)."}]}

findings.title: Compilation error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without required UserModel argument
findings.body: The condition `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` invokes the method with zero arguments, but the only method available in `UsernamePasswordForm` (the parent class) is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. There is no no-arg overload defined anywhere in the codebase, so this line fails to compile and the PR cannot be built. The caller almost certainly meant `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys UI not initialized on initial (user-less) login
findings.body: The new check `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))` relies on a helper that includes `user != null` in its predicate. As a result `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never invoked when the user has not yet been identified on the first visit to the username/password form. The pre-PR code (inside the `else` branch) unconditionally called `fillContextForm` when `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`, which is the behavior the existing test `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest#passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` (and the equivalent test in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest`) still relies on. Both tests assert that `//form[@id='webauth']` is present and that `usernameAutocomplete` equals `"username webauthn"` on the very first login page before any user is set, so this regression will make those tests fail. The intent of the PR is to add passkey support for re-authentication (user already present), not to remove it for the initial login. The fix is to gate `fillContextForm` on `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` only, dropping the user-presence requirement (or splitting the helper into a realm-level predicate and a user-level predicate).
